title: Nilpotent radical and semisimple quotient of a left Artinian ring
statement: Let $R$ be a unital ring, not necessarily commutative, that is left Artinian: every descending sequence of left ideals eventually stabilizes. Let $J$ be its Jacobson radical, the intersection of all maximal left ideals (the intersection is $R$ if there are none). Then $J$ is a two-sided ideal, $J^h=0$ for some integer $h\geq0$, and $R/J$ is semisimple. Here a ring is semisimple when its regular left module is a sum of simple left ideals, and a left module is simple [def-weil-pbc-simple-module] when it is nonzero and has no nonzero proper submodule.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.4.7, first reduction, p. 307: Jacobson radical and semisimple quotient; the proof cites Lam 1991, section 4.
